requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game.
How the selected Pods are distributed between Sections A and B.
The starting orientation of the Pods.
The exact tokens initially placed in the Intruder bag.
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next-numbered in Section B, then alternate A/B (so the third goes in A). 3. All Pods start Locked side up. 4. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player in the bag. At four players that is 7 Adults, 14 tokens total.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Setup states: “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. Return the rest to the box.” 4. Setup states: “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player. Place the remaining Intruder tokens and the Intruder Carcass tokens next to the board.” Inference: four players therefore means 3 + 4 = 7 Adult tokens and 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 7 = 14 tokens in total.

requested_parts: How Objectives are filtered by player count.
How many of each type are dealt and their secrecy.
When players choose between their Objectives and what happens to the rejected card.
Whether Eggs trigger the choice.
answers.answer: 1. Let P equal the actual player count and remove from both the Corporate and Personal decks every Objective requiring more than P players. 2. Shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one Corporate and one Personal Objective, kept hidden. 3. Players do not choose one during the initial deal: when the first Intruder miniature of any type appears on the board, every player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other from the game face down; nobody may look at another player's removed Objective. 4. Eggs are not Intruders, so they do not trigger that choice.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Setup says: “Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden. (You receive Objectives before the Character draft on purpose — pick a Character suited to your Objective.)” 3–4. Critical gameplay moments says: “First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

requested_parts: The cards discarded to pay for an Action card with printed cost 2 in the stated hand scenario.
Whether Contamination cards can substitute for Action-card payment.
How to handle an Action card with OR effects.
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself plus the two other Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2; that is 3 Action cards total. The two Contamination cards are not used as payment. 2. Contamination cards cannot replace any Action cards in the payment. 3. If the card has two sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect; the played card and its printed-cost payment still apply.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Action Cost says: “For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.” It also says: “Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” The example states: “Captain's Basic Repairs has an extra cost of 2. Discard Basic Repairs itself + 2 other Action cards = 3 Action cards total. Those three cards are sufficient for its printed Action-card payment; Contamination cannot replace any of them.” Inference: the stated cost-2 card plus the two other Action cards satisfy the payment exactly. 3. The Action-card rules say: “To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one.”

requested_parts: When the Character suffers Fire damage after taking one Action and passing.
Whether the Character may take normal Actions again this Player Phase.
Whether cards may be discarded on passing.
Whether later players' rounds cause additional Fire wounds to this passed Character.
answers.answer: 1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions for the rest of this Player Phase, though the general rule allows an Interruption card after passing subject to its requirements. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. No: later players' rounds do not give a passed Character further Fire wounds that turn; Fire is checked at the end of that Character's own round.
answers.evidence: 1, 4. Turn Structure says: “A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn).” The passing table says: “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.” FAQ says: “Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.” 2. The passing table says: “Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below.” It also says: “You may still play Interruption after passing, subject to its usual card requirements (FAQ Rules 21).” 3. The passing table says: “At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.”

requested_parts: What happens to an unexplored Room tile and its Item Counter on entry.
How its Exploration effect and token are resolved.
When and where the ordinary Movement Noise roll occurs, and how Silence/Danger affect it.
What happens to a Noise marker when its Corridor already has one.
How an already occupied destination affects the Movement Noise roll.
answers.answer: 1. On entering a face-down Room, flip the tile face up and reveal its Exploration token. The token's number sets the Item Counter for ordinary Rooms by rotating the tile until that number faces the board's Item Counter symbol; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime have no Item count. 2. Resolve the revealed effect, then remove the Exploration token from the game into the box. A Door effect places a Door token in the Corridor used to enter. 3. After exploration, make the ordinary Noise roll only if the destination has no Character or Intruder; the resulting number places a Noise marker in the corresponding connected Corridor (including a Technical Corridors Entrance if applicable). A Silence Exploration result replaces the Noise roll with no effect (unless the mover has Slime, when it resolves as Danger). A Danger result replaces the roll and moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination; if none are eligible, place Noise markers in each connected Corridor lacking one (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance). 4. If the numbered Corridor already has a Noise marker, resolve an Encounter instead of placing a second marker there. 5. If any Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Movement rules state: “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box; (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” Exploration tokens state: “The token's front shows (1) a number = the amount of Items obtainable in that Room, and (2) a special effect symbol.” And: “the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.” Doors effect: “place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.” Token handling: “After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).” 3. Movement rules state: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.” Exploration effects state: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 4. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 5. Noise rules state: “Remember: never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement's Action-card cost.
What Careful Movement replaces and where it places Noise.
When Careful Movement is forbidden, including destination Corridor availability.
Whether it can cross Closed Doors and whether a miniature can stop in a Corridor.
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2. It follows normal Movement restrictions but replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing one Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room entered. It also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that chosen Noise placement. 3. It cannot be used in Combat or if every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker. 4. No: Closed Doors block passage for player Movement, including Careful Movement; a miniature can never stop in a Corridor, only in a Room.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Basic Actions says: “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.” 4. Movement rules state: “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.” Also: “A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement.”

requested_parts: What happens when a Noise roll calls for a Corridor that already has Noise.
Which connected Noise markers are removed and when.
How the Encounter draws and handles its token, including Blank versus non-Blank destinations.
How Surprise Attack is determined and whether Contamination cards count.
answers.answer: 1. Since a Corridor cannot hold a second Noise marker, the attempted placement triggers an Encounter. 2. At the start of the Encounter, discard all Noise markers from Corridors connected to the Character's Room, including the Technical Corridors space because this Room has an Entrance. 3. Draw one Intruder token. If it is non-Blank, keep it aside outside the bag and place its matching miniature in the Room; it remains aside unless a rule returns it, such as that Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. If it is Blank, instead place Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without an Intruder appearing. 4. For a non-Blank token, compare its number with the number of cards in the triggering player's hand: fewer cards than that number causes a Surprise Attack. Action and Contamination cards both count, so the two Contamination cards in hand contribute to the comparison.
answers.evidence: 1. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 2–3. Encounter rules state: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).” They continue: “Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below.” “Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room.” “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” Technical Corridors rules state: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board.” 4. Encounter rules state: “Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.” The Quick Reference likewise says the drawn non-Blank token is kept aside “until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: How Danger resolves when several eligible neighboring Intruders are present.
What happens when no eligible neighboring Intruders are present.
Whether moving an Intruder into the Character's Room through Danger is an Encounter.
How Slime changes a Silence result.
answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are no eligible Intruders, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. 3. No. An Intruder that merely moves into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it simply leaves them in Combat. 4. If the Character has a Slime marker, a Silence result is resolved as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Exploration rules state: “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 3. Encounter rules state: “An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).” 4. Exploration rules state: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” Noise rules likewise say: “Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.”

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank token when an Encounter draws Blank.
When bag development adds an Adult after an Encounter Blank.
How Blank behaves during Intruder bag development.
answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in every Corridor connected to the Room; return the Blank to the bag, and no miniature appears. 2. Add one Adult to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag and an Adult token is available; otherwise add none. 3. During bag development, Blank instead adds one Adult token if any are available, with no last-token condition, then the Blank itself is returned to the bag.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Encounter rules state: “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” 3. Intruder bag development says: “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.” Inference: the bag-development rule does not include the Encounter rule's condition that the Blank be the last token in the bag.

requested_parts: Where two Intruders end when attempting to move together through the same Closed Door.
What happens to the Closed Door and whether it may later be closed again.
Whether a Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Closed Door is blocked.
answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders remain in the Room they attempted to leave. 2. They destroy the Closed Door simultaneously, leaving its token lying to represent a Destroyed Door. It cannot later be closed by ordinary Door-closing effects; only the Plasma Torch Item can close a Destroyed Door. 3. No. An Intruder appearing through a Corridor as a result of a Noise roll appears regardless of a Closed Door.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Door rules state: “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put).” They also state: “Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.” 3. Door rules state: “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

requested_parts: What happens to an injured Intruder's miniature, Injury markers and token when it enters Technical Corridors where Noise is already present.
Whether the Noise marker is removed.
Whether Characters and Doors can normally use Technical Corridors.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature from the board, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. 2. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is not removed. 3. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans Item. Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Technical Corridors rules state: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.” 3. The same section says: “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's "Technical Corridors" Action card and the "Technical Corridor Plans" Item card).” It also states: “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Action-card costs for Shoot and Melee.
Shoot's Weapon, Ammo and target requirements.
Melee's Contamination card handling and target requirements.
What happens on a miss for each Action.
How a double-hit result resolves for Shoot versus Melee.
answers.answer: 1. Each is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card. 2. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo; choose one Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon, and roll the Combat die. 3. For Melee, draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile, choose an Intruder in your Room, and roll the die. 4. An ordinary Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and gives the shooter no Wound. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and gives the attacker 1 Serious Wound. 5. A double-hit result normally deals 2 Injuries in Shoot, before Weapon modifiers; in Melee it deals 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: 1. The Basic Actions heading says: “Basic Actions (available to every Character; cost 1 Action card, except Careful Movement which costs 2).” 2–3. Combat rules state: “Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo. (1) Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; (2) discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; (3) roll the Combat die.” They state: “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die.” 4. The summary states: “Ordinary attack misses: a Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.” 5. Combat table states: “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type.”

requested_parts: How Larva death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How Adult death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How Queen death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How a Retreat arrow on the Queen's Injury Effect check changes the outcome.
answers.answer: 1. Compare the Larva's current total Injuries: 1 Injury kills it; remove its miniature and place no Carcass. 2. Draw 1 Intruder Attack card and use its blood value only; if blood is less than or equal to current total Injuries the Adult dies, otherwise it lives. On death remove its miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Attack cards and sum their blood values; if the sum is less than or equal to current total Injuries she dies, otherwise she lives. On death remove her miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 4. If either card drawn for the Queen has the Retreat arrow, she retreats instead of resolving a numerical death/endurance result: draw an Event card, move her via the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Intruder Injuries and death says to compare “current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” The table states: “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass”; “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; and “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.” 4. Retreat rules state: “during an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card's Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When Escape attacks resolve and how many occur, including their order.
Who is targeted by the attacks during Escape.
Where the Character's Corpse stays if they die.
What follows if they survive into an empty unexplored destination.
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room; resolve larger Intruders first in this order: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. 2. Each Escape attack targets the escaping Character. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4. If they survive, complete the move into the neighboring Room; since it is unexplored, explore it normally, then make a Noise roll because it is empty (unless a Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces that roll).
answers.evidence: 1, 3–4. Character Escape states: “to leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” 2. Intruder Attack rules state: “An Escape attack targets the escaper.” The Intruder attack target rule says: “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” For unexplored movement, the Movement rules state: “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” Inference: an empty unexplored destination meets the stated condition for the usual post-move Noise roll, except when exploration replaces it.

requested_parts: How the target is chosen when several Characters are in the Room and how a tie is broken.
How an ordinary Intruder Attack hits or misses.
What changes for a Larva attack.
Where the Contamination card gained from Larva attack is placed.
answers.answer: 1. Target the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; a tie goes to the Character with the First Player token or the next player in turn order. 2. For an Intruder other than Larva, draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder-type symbol means resolve its effect; a nonmatching symbol means the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon for attacks, then discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card; instead it is removed from the board and placed on the target's Character board, and that Character gains 1 Contamination card. If they already have a Larva, the attacker disappears, the existing Larva stays, and the Character gains only the Contamination card without automatically dying. 4. A Contamination card is placed on top of that Character's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Intruder Attack rules state: “Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).” For non-Larvae: “draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. Discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile; if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck.” 3. Infest says: “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” 4. Contamination rules state: “When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing one Serious Wound prevents death from a Light Wound when at three Serious Wounds.
What a third Light Wound does otherwise.
What Heal removes.
Where the Corpse and Heavy Objects go upon death.
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing makes the Serious Wound's effect ignored but it still counts toward the three-wound limit; with 3 Serious Wounds, any additional Light or Serious Wound causes instant death even if one is dressed. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room, and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: 1–4. Wounds rules state: “Light Wounds: track on your Character board — 1st marker on the upper space, 2nd on the lower space (= 2 Light Wounds); on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” They state: “Death: a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.” Dressing and healing rules state: “Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds. Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen and Shower scan.
Which scanned cards those Rooms remove and how they handle Infected cards/Larvae.
Which cards Surgery scans and removes and how it handles a Larva.
Surgery's Action cost, wound and passing/shuffle consequences.
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower may scan all Contamination cards in your hand only. 2. They remove all non-Infected scanned cards. An Infected result keeps the card and places a Larva on your Character board; if you already had a Larva, you die and a Creeper appears in the Room. The Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes your Slime marker. 3. Surgery scans all your Contamination cards in your deck, hand and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva from your board if present. 4. Surgery is a Room Action costing 2 Action cards; after it, suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, and shuffle all your cards (including your entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Room Actions list Canteen: “Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room).” Shower Room: “discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen).” Canteen/Shower scan outcomes state: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result”; “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.” 3–4. Surgery Room Action says: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” Common Room Action requirements say: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.”

requested_parts: How Shoot and Melee destroy uncarried Eggs, including Melee miss exceptions.
How Grenades and Molotov destroy uncarried Eggs.
How Fire destroys Eggs and when the Nest is destroyed.
When and where Noise is rolled for each attack attempt.
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys one uncarried Egg. For Egg Melee, a successful attack still draws one Contamination card to the Action discard pile; a miss causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. 2. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately. An uncarried Egg lets its Room be targeted as if an Intruder were there. 3. A Fire marker normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg in each Event Phase Fire Damage step; if the Nest Egg pool has Vulnerability to Fire, it destroys 2 per step. The Nest is destroyed when no Eggs remain, whether carried away or destroyed; mark it with 1 Injury marker. 4. After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise, including after a miss. For a Grenade/Molotov thrown remotely, roll in your own Room, not in the Nest.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Egg rules state: “Egg tokens on the Intruder board represent the Eggs in the Nest; taking or destroying Eggs removes them from the Intruder board. When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.” The Egg destruction table says: “Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.” “Grenade | Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.” “Molotov Cocktail | Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.” “Fire marker | Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).” Egg Melee rules state: “a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.” 4. Noise rules state: “after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).” Inference: any Egg destruction that reaches zero remaining Eggs destroys the Nest under the quoted rule.

requested_parts: What Pod conditions permit or prevent boarding and the Action cost/location.
What must be resolved before boarding and when the attempt fails.
Pod capacity and whether Heavy Objects use a space.
What a boarded Character may do while waiting and the consequences of those options.
answers.answer: 1. To enter a Pod, use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action in the matching Section; pay 2 Action cards, be in that Room, be outside Combat with no Malfunction there, and choose an Unlocked Pod with a free Character space. No entry is allowed while the Section has an Intruder or Malfunction. 2. First roll Noise; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section Room, the attempt fails; otherwise board. 3. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not take Character spaces. 4. After boarding you may launch immediately: remove Pod and occupants' miniatures from game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth, but still face Contamination and Objective checks. If you wait, you pass the current turn and remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. On your first round of each later Player Phase, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass, launch, or exit free to the Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Evacuation Section A/B Room Action says: “try to enter an Unlocked Escape Pod with space in that Section: make a Noise roll; if any Intruder appears (or is present) in this Room, the attempt fails; otherwise board the Pod (2 spaces per Pod).” Escape Pod rules say: “Board: pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail.” Common requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.” 3–4. Escape Pod rules state: “Capacity: 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.” “Launch immediately: after boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.” “Wait after boarding: you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1).” Waiting options: “Start of your first round in each later Player Phase | Choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2).”

requested_parts: The order of the endgame checks.
The result of two Damaged Engines.
The effects of a non-Earth destination, including the Quarantine Objective at Mars.
The Contamination check for an infected survivor versus a survivor carrying a Larva.
Whether launched Pod passengers undergo Contamination checks.
answers.answer: 1. Resolve Engines, then Coordinates, then Contamination, then Objectives. 2. Two Damaged Engines meet the 2-or-3 threshold and make the ship explode; everything aboard dies, but launched Pod passengers are already away. 3. A non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters while the ship itself is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. 4. For a surviving Character with no Larva, scan every Contamination card in the Action deck, hand and discard. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw. If at least one is Infected, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into one new Action deck and draw the top four; any Contamination card among them kills, whether Infected or not. A Character who already has a Larva skips the initial scan but undergoes that same shuffle/draw check. 5. Yes. Every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers, undergoes the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: 1. Victory Check says: “Resolve Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives in that order.” 2–3. It states: “2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Launched Pod passengers are already away.” It further states: “Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars.” 4–5. Contamination check rules say: “Contamination, for every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers: No Larva already on board: Scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw.” They continue: “At least one Infected card, OR a Larva already on board: shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into a single new Action deck and draw the top 4 cards. Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not; four Action cards with no Contamination means you survive this check. A Larva skips the initial Scan but still requires this complete shuffle, draw and result check.”
